deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues the previous page's series 'Schwingungen des Stabes A in der Sternwarte' ('oscillations of bar A in the observatory'). It is an observation of a magnet bar (magnetometer) swinging under the earth's field. Times are read on a chronometer, which the previous page compares with the Shelton clock: chronometer 11h10'0" = 11h32'7" Shelton. The fragment 'llon' in the left margin belongs to the facing page. The adopted approximate period is P = 12.87 s, and swing n = 0 passed at T0 = 11h2'57.30".

(1) Column layout. Column 1 is the swing number n. Column 2 is the observed passage time t_n; hours and minutes are written only when they change. The prefixes 0, 1, 2, 3 mean 12h, 13h, 14h, 15h, because the hour count restarts after noon.

(2) Column 3 is the reduced epoch r_n = t_n - n*P, written as seconds after 11h02m. If P were exact and constant, r_n would equal 57.30 for every n.

Examples (my arithmetic, times in seconds after 11h):
- n = 187: 187*12.87 = 2406.69 s = 40m6.69s; 2583.46 - 2406.69 = 176.77, written 56.77.
- n = 407: 5414.30 - 5238.09 = 176.21. This requires the observed time to be 14.30 (see corrections).
- n = 583: 7679.10 - 7503.21 = 175.89.
- n = 987: 12878.42 - 12702.69 = 175.73.
- n = 1103: 14372.26 - 14195.61 = 176.65.

The reduced epochs run 57.30 (n=0) -> about 57.2 (n about 105) -> about 56.83 (n about 190) -> about 56.35 (n about 410) -> about 55.84 (n about 585) -> about 55.8 (n about 988) -> about 56.6 (n about 1105).
- The mean true period over the whole run is P = 12.87 - (57.30 - 56.69)/1111 ≈ 12.8695 s (my computation).
- The non-monotonic drift shows that the period was not constant. It changed with amplitude and with time variations of the magnetic field and temperature.
- Gauss would combine groups of r_n, for example the means of each block, to get the period by least-squares-type averaging. The horizontal rules under 587 and 989 mark such groups.

(3) Side numbers. At n = 987 he writes 648.242 and 77.983; at n = 1104 he writes 646.10 and 58.20.
- The previous page has 644.25 with 859.5 and 856.5 at n = 107 and 108.
- These pairs are scale readings: the equilibrium (rest) position of the bar and the swing amplitude in scale divisions.

(4) 'Decr. log. 0,00117' is the common-log decrement of the amplitude per swing.
- My check: [log10(859.5) - log10(58.20)]/(1104 - 107) = 1.16932/997 = 0.0011728.
- With 856.5 at n = 108: 1.16779/996 = 0.0011725.
- Both round to 0.00117, so he evidently took the decrement over the whole interval.
- Partial intervals give 0.001184 (107 to 987) and 0.001086 (987 to 1104), showing the damping is not perfectly exponential.
- The previous page's 0.00133 checks the same way: log10(1071.8/742.767)/119.5 = 0.001333.

Purpose: the period of the bar and its logarithmic decrement are needed to reduce the period to infinitely small arcs and to correct for damping. This feeds the absolute determination of horizontal intensity (the m*T product) in Gauss's magnetic program. The torsion determination on the previous page belongs to the same procedure.
errors: n=197: from the written time 11h45'12.20" the reduced value is 56.81, not 56.79 as written (discrepancy 0.02; either the time was 12.18 or an arithmetic slip).
n=198: 25.08 - 28.26 gives 56.82, but 56.86 is written (discrepancy 0.04). Alternatively the time is misread and should be 25.12.
n=407: the transcribed time 14.36 would give 56.27. The written 56.21 corresponds to 14.30, which is very probably what the manuscript has.
n=989: 4.28 - 8.43 gives 55.85. The value transcribed as 55.89 is either a slip or a misreading of 55.85.

n=1104, 1107, 1110, 1111: the computed values are 56.60, 56.53, 56.66, 56.71. Each written value (56.58, 56.51, 56.64, 56.69) is 0.02 lower. This is a constant offset, likely from accumulating 12.87 from a slightly wrong starting value, or a misread base. Its effect on the period is negligible.
None of these affect the logarithmic decrement 0.00117, which checks correctly.

results.what: Reduction of a long series of magnet oscillation passages to epochs t_n - n*P with an approximate period, to determine the oscillation period precisely and detect its drift
results.modern_name: Method of coincidences / reduced epochs (O-C residuals) for period determination
results.usually_credited_to: Standard astronomical practice; for magnetometers, Gauss and Weber (1832-1840)

results.what: Logarithmic decrement of amplitude per oscillation, [log10 A_m - log10 A_n]/(n-m) = 0.00117
results.modern_name: Logarithmic decrement (damping) of a damped oscillator
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber in the Göttingen magnetic work (Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins, 1836-1841)

results.what: Recording of the rest position and amplitude in scale divisions for the reduction to infinitely small arcs
results.modern_name: Amplitude (finite-arc) correction of the pendulum/magnetometer period
results.usually_credited_to: Standard (pendulum theory); applied to magnetometers by Gauss 1832

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine observational log of magnetometer oscillations with a standard reduction and a logarithmic decrement. It is exactly the kind of material known from Gauss's published and unpublished magnetic work of the 1830s. Nothing here is mathematically novel.

checkable.asserts: n=197 with time 45m12.20s gives reduced epoch 56.81, not the written 56.79.
n=407 with time 1h30m14.30s (from 11h) gives 56.21 as written, supporting the reading 14.30.
n=987: 3h34m38.42s - 987*12.87 s gives the reduced epoch 55.73.
The log decrement from amplitude 859.5 (n=107) to 58.20 (n=1104) is about 0.00117 per swing.
Previous page's decrement 0.00133 from amplitude about 1071.8 (n about 2.5) to 742.767 (n=122).
The mean period over swings 0 to 1111 is about 12.86945 s.

transcription_corrections: n=407: the time should read 0.30.14.30 (12h30m14.30s), not 14.36; the written reduced value 56.21 confirms 14.30.
n=989: the reduced value is probably 55.85 (computed), not 55.89; the digit is ambiguous in the image.
The hour prefixes 0, 1, 2, 3 mean 12h, 13h, 14h, 15h on the chronometer (continuing from 11h), and n=584 '8 11.94' means 1h8m11.94s.
Horizontal rules appear under the reduced values of 587 and 989 (and a short mark at 1104), grouping the blocks used for means.
'llon' in the left margin belongs to the facing page (probably the end of 'Shelton'), not to this page.
